citation.authors: van Leeuwen WMA, Hublin C, Sallinen M, Harma M, Hirvonen A, Porkka-Heiskanen T
citation.title: Prolonged Sleep Restriction Affects Glucose Metabolism in Healthy Young Men

population.description: Twenty-three healthy young men aged 19-29 (enrolment range; mean 23.1, SD 2.5), screened by examination, blood tests and polysomnography; 15 in the experimental group, 8 controls. BMI is given per group (prestudy mean and SD) and entered in each protocol; age is the pooled value.

protocols.name: baseline_night_con
protocols.description: Control (CON) group, baseline night: 8 h in bed every night (the paper gives no clock hours for CON; 23:00-07:00 as for EXP is assumed; minutes 0-479 of the arm), blood drawn 07:30 before the 08:00 breakfast, 10 h after the last food (minute 510). Last food was the 21:30 snack (200 kcal, composition not printed) and is not entered as a meal; prefast_hours 1.5 = 23:00 minus 21:30, derived and assumed.

protocols.name: baseline_night_exp
protocols.description: Experimental (EXP, before restriction) group, baseline night: in bed 23:00-07:00 (8 h in bed; minutes 0-479 of the arm), blood drawn 07:30 before the 08:00 breakfast, 10 h after the last food (minute 510). Last food was the 21:30 snack (200 kcal, composition not printed) and is not entered as a meal; prefast_hours 1.5 = 23:00 minus 21:30, derived and assumed.

left_out.what: fasting glucose, insulin, leptin after five nights of 4 h in bed and after two recovery nights, EXP group (Table 2, SR and REC columns): the arm needs five days of standardized meals whose macronutrient composition is not printed, with sleep debt carried across days
meals of the study days (breakfast 600, lunch 800, dinner 700 kcal, snacks 300 and 200 kcal): energy only, no grams of carbohydrate, fat or protein
CON group SR and REC columns (Table 2): samples at 07:30 on the corresponding later nights, after days of standardized laboratory meals whose grams are not printed
clock time of the salivary cortisol peak, Table 1 and Results 3.1 (salivary cortisol, not the model's serum cortisol)
changes expressed as percent of each person's own baseline (Results 3.2, 3.3): not a difference in the marker's unit
